paragraphs: Abba Yose HaChorem: Sifra, Emor, and Menachot 37a. Rashi explains HaChorem: his nose was sunken. Tosafot write that it is a place-name, for how could one give him a derogatory epithet? Sheerit Yaakov writes: Bekhorot 43a says a charum is one whose nose is sunken, and so forth. Rabbi Yose says a charum is only someone who can apply kohl to both eyes at once. They told him: ‘You have gone too far.’ End. Thus perhaps he was called Rabbi Yose HaChorem because he stated the law concerning a charum, as a sign that this Rabbi Yose was the one who said that law, known to them in the study house. End quotation.
